text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Nigeria earns more than expected from crude oil sales.
- National plan to respond to oil spillages has been formulated and will soon be considered by government.
- State-run Nigerian Electric Power Authority rehabilitates 40 substations in the Lagos area in an ongoing programme of improving power supplies.
- Government says manufacturers are charging too much for their products.

- Finance Minister Anthony Ani discloses that government may take "Golden Shares" in more than just the big four banks (UBA, UBN, First Bank, Afribank). Sources say a decree allowing the "Golden Shares" has already been drafted, giving government the right to appoint or dismiss directors from institutions regardless of the level of its investment.
